title: Vice President, Operational Risk
description: Why this role is important for us The Vice President, Operational Risk is a senior First Line of Defense (1LoD) role responsible for strengthening operational risk management and the control environment across the business. The role partners with business leaders and process owners to identify and assess risks, establish effective controls, monitor emerging risks, and drive timely remediation of control gaps and issues. What you will be responsible for As Operational Risk, Vice President you will: Partner with business leaders to identify, assess, and manage operational risks. Lead and support Risk and Control Self-Assessments (RCSAs) and ongoing risk assessments. Evaluate control design and effectiveness and identify opportunities to strengthen the control environment. Develop and monitor Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), risk thresholds, and management reporting. Analyze operational incidents, control failures, and emerging risks, including performing root cause analysis. Drive remediation of risk and control issues, ensuring actions address underlying root causes. Provide risk oversight and challenge for new products, processes, technology implementations, and business change. Prepare and present risk reporting to senior management and governance forums. Partner with Compliance, Operational Risk, Internal Audit, and other oversight functions while reinforcing clear first-line ownership and accountability. Promote a strong risk culture and proactive identification and escalation of risk. Education & Preferred Qualifications Strong experience in operational risk, business risk and controls, operations, audit, compliance, or internal controls, preferably within financial services. Experience with RCSAs, control design, KRIs, issue management, remediation, and root cause analysis. Strong analytical skills with the ability to identify risks and translate them into practical business controls. Proven ability to influence and constructively challenge senior stakeholders. Strong written, verbal, and executive-level communication skills. Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant professional experience. Salary Range: $115,000 - $201,250 Annual The range quoted above applies to the role in the primary location specified. If the candidate would ultimately work outside of the primary location above, the applicable range could differ. Employees are eligible to participate in State Street’s comprehensive benefits program, which includes: our retirement savings plan (401K) with company match; insurance coverage including basic life, medical, dental, vision, long-term disability, and other optional additional coverages; paid-time off including vacation, sick leave, short term disability, and family care responsibilities; access to our Employee Assistance Program; incentive compensation including eligibility for annual performance-based awards (excluding certain sales roles subject to sales incentive plans); and, eligibility for certain tax advantaged savings plans. For a full overview, visit https://hrportal.ehr.com/statestreet/Home . About State Street Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are essential to our continued success. We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. As an essential partner in our shared success, you’ll benefit from inclusive development opportunities, flexible work-life support, paid volunteer days, and vibrant employee networks that keep you connected to what matters most. Join us in shaping the future. title: Manager, Business Process Risk & Controls
description: We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time. Position Summary: The Manager, Business Process Risk & Controls is responsible for supporting second-line oversight of business process controls across CVS Health’s Internal Control over Financial Reporting (ICFR) environment. Reporting to the Lead Director, Business Process Risk & Controls, this role will help execute the governance framework, oversight activities, and continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen the effectiveness, consistency, and sustainability of business process controls across CVS Health’s business segments and functional organizations. This individual contributor role operates independently, providing recommendations and influencing decision-making while partnering closely with business process control owners, Internal Audit, External Audit, and cross-functional leadership teams. As a key member of the SOX Compliance Hub, this role will help drive the organization’s vision to establish a proactive, scalable, and efficient control environment that inspires confidence across the enterprise. Key Responsibilities Business Process Control Governance & Oversight Execute enterprise governance standards and methodologies for business process controls. Support the development and implementation of control oversight strategies and operating procedures. Evaluate business process control environments and identify opportunities to improve effectiveness and consistency. Perform independent assessments of control design and execution across business segments and functional organizations. Provide recommendations to improve control sustainability and reduce operational complexity. Support the implementation of standardized control practices across the enterprise. Second-Line Oversight & Challenge Provide objective challenge to management regarding business process control design, operation, and remediation activities. Review risk assessments, control frameworks, and control documentation to identify potential gaps or emerging risks. Monitor control environment performance and identify trends requiring escalation or additional oversight. Support issue identification, root-cause analysis, and remediation planning activities. Escalate significant risks and observations to SOX Compliance Hub leadership, as appropriate. Deficiency Management & Remediation Support governance activities related to business process control deficiencies. Evaluate remediation plans and challenge management to ensure sustainable solutions are implemented. Monitor remediation progress and validate the effectiveness of corrective actions. Assist in developing reporting and dashboards that provide visibility into control performance and remediation status. Audit & Regulatory Support Serve as a liaison with Internal Audit and External Audit for assigned business process areas. Support management’s annual SOX 404 assessment activities. Coordinate information requests, walkthroughs, testing activities, and remediation efforts. Assist with enterprise audit readiness activities and control environment assessments. Transformation & Continuous Improvement Support initiatives focused on: Control optimization and rationalization Process standardization GRC technology enablement Data-driven monitoring and reporting Continuous controls improvement Partner with Finance, Operations, Technology, and business leaders to modernize and simplify the control environment. Identify opportunities to enhance control efficiency while maintaining appropriate risk coverage. Governance & Reporting Prepare materials and reporting for: Control Champion Forums Senior Leadership Updates Internal Audit and External Audit meetings Deficiency governance discussions Quarterly risk and control reporting Assist in developing meaningful metrics and KPIs that provide insight into control performance and emerging risks. Leadership Scope This position primarily functions as an individual contributor while influencing a broad group of stakeholders across the organization. Indirect Influence Business Process Control Owners Business Process Control Performers Finance Leadership Teams Segment Leaders Functional Leaders Internal Audit External Audit Technology and Transformation Teams May provide informal guidance, coaching, and work direction to junior team members and cross-functional partners. title: Lead - Security Controls Assurance - SOX
description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic's Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team is the connective tissue that holds the company accountable to its security and control commitments. We translate regulatory, customer, and voluntary obligations into controls that teams act on, and give leadership a bird's-eye view of how well we're meeting them. We're building toward continuous assurance, to challenge and evidence the performance of controls continuously rather than through periodic audits. As Anthropic scales to meet public-company standards, the Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) control environment over our technology stack is one of the most consequential things this team owns. As part of Security GRC's technical controls assurance function, you will be the voice on what the IT general controls must achieve to support SOX 404 compliance. In partnership with Internal Audit, you will define control requirements and acceptance criteria for the in-scope engineering systems and infrastructure that underpin financial reporting. You will pair with engineering as they design and implement against those requirements, and validate that what ships actually meets the bar before Internal Audit and our external auditors test it. You are the product owner for control design methodology and continuous control monitoring, initially around ITGCs, but extending into other areas of security and compliance to drive visibility where and when we need it.  Key responsibilities Define control requirements and acceptance criteria across the core ITGC domains of logical access, change management, computer operations, and program development for SOX in-scope systems, including home-built platforms where the control has to be designed into the system rather than bolted on. Set the bar for in-scope systems from day one. As financially significant systems are built, migrated, or replaced, define what the system must provide (auditability, segregation of duties, change control, immutable logging, evidence retention) before go-live, so controls are not retrofitted after the fact. Pressure-test changes for SOX impact during design. Review major infrastructure, system, and agent framework changes for control impact while decisions are still cheap, and maintain a clear view of which changes alter the SOX scope, key control population, or evidence requirements. Own second-line control monitoring and evidence readiness. Stand up continuous controls monitoring and automated evidence collection for ITGCs (control testing, walkthrough preparation, population and completeness validation, and mapping to the common controls framework). Materially raise automated evidence coverage and cut audit prep time. Drive control deficiency remediation with cross functional partners. Track and root-cause ITGC deficiencies surfaced by monitoring, Internal Audit, or external audit; partner with engineering owners on remediation design; and assess whether remediation actually closes the gap before re-testing. Assess scope changes through a SOX lens. When new products, entities, systems, or integrations come into scope, provide technical and compliance assessment of their impact on control design, evidence requirements, and engineering effort before commitments are made. Maintain alignment with the broader compliance portfolio. Where SOX ITGCs overlap with SOC 2, ISO 27001/42001, or other frameworks, ensure controls are designed once and evidenced once, and that changes made for one framework do not silently break another. Minimum qualifications Thrive at the pace of a hypergrowth company. You're comfortable making calls with incomplete information and reprioritizing as scope shifts. Have led or been a senior contributor to an ITGC program through SOX 404 readiness and/or at a public company, with a working command of PCAOB AS 2201, COSO 2013, and how external auditors scope, test, and evaluate technology controls and deficiencies. Have genuine engineering fluency, possibly from an earlier engineering career: you can read code and Terraform, follow a CI/CD pipeline end to end, and challenge a design on its technical merits. Have programming skills in Python or at least one systems language such as Go, Rust, or C/C++. Have deep familiarity with developer platform, release engineering, cloud infrastructure, or ERP/financial systems control domains. Understand the role of the second line: you can advise and challenge engineering without taking ownership of their controls, and you know where the line sits between your monitoring and Internal Audit's independent testing. title: Compliance Manager, Monitoring & Investigations
description: About the company Hi, we're Ondo Finance. Our mission is to provide institutional-grade, blockchain-enabled investment products and services. We have both a technology arm that develops decentralized finance technology, and an asset management arm that creates and manages tokenized funds. We were the first company to tokenize exposure to US Treasuries, and have since expanded into several other assets. We are also focused on incubating protocols that can support both tokenized real-world assets and traditional crypto. Founded by folks from Goldman Sachs Digital Assets Team, we’re backed by some of the best investors in the world including Founders Fund, Coinbase Ventures, Pantera Capital, Tiger Global, and more. We are currently the leaders in the space in terms of AUM and are well capitalized to continue growing the firm. We're fully remote, with team members across the U.S. About the Role We're looking for a Compliance Manager to lead and strengthen our monitoring and investigations program across both fiat and on-chain activity. You'll own transaction monitoring, secondary market and trade surveillance, investigations, and regulatory reporting, and you'll be a key partner to Legal, Product, Engineering, and Operations as we scale. This role suits a hands-on investigator who's equally comfortable tracing funds through a blockchain explorer, analyzing trading patterns for manipulation, and writing a SAR narrative that holds up to regulatory scrutiny. Responsibilities Own the day-to-day transaction monitoring program for fiat and digital asset flows, including alert review, escalation, and disposition. Design, tune, and document monitoring rules and scenarios based on the firm's risk assessment, typologies, and emerging threats. Use blockchain analytics tools to assess wallet exposure, counterparty risk, and illicit-finance indicators such as sanctions, mixers, darknet markets, scams, and ransomware. Track alert volumes, false-positive rates, and SLAs, and drive improvements in efficiency and coverage. Build and run surveillance for trading activity on primary and secondary markets, including on-chain transfers, DEX/CEX activity, and OTC flows. Detect and investigate potential market abuse, including wash trading, spoofing, layering, front-running, pump-and-dump schemes, and insider trading. Work with Engineering and Data teams on surveillance tooling, data pipelines, and alert logic. Maintain reporting procedures, quality control checks, and audit-ready documentation. Support regulatory exams, independent audits, and responses to regulator inquiries. Requirements 5+ years of experience in financial crimes compliance, with significant hands-on work in investigations, AML/BSA, and transaction monitoring. Demonstrated experience with blockchain analytics tools such as Chainalysis (Reactor, KYT), TRM Labs, or Elliptic, and the ability to trace funds independently on-chain. Strong working knowledge of the BSA, USA PATRIOT Act, FinCEN guidance, and OFAC sanctions requirements. A track record of writing high-quality SAR narratives and investigation reports. Strong analytical skills, with the ability to work with large datasets and spot anomalous patterns. Excellent written and verbal communication, sound judgment, and the ability to handle sensitive matters with discretion. Nice to Have Experience with trade surveillance or market abuse detection at a broker-dealer, exchange, ATS, or digital asset trading venue. Familiarity with securities regulations (SEC, FINRA) and how they apply to tokenized assets or digital securities. Experience building or scaling a monitoring program at a high-growth fintech or crypto company. Experience managing or mentoring analysts. Certifications such as CAMS, CCAS, CFE, or CCI. What we offer Competitive compensation including but not limited to salary, future token rights, and/or equity (according to your preferences) — We are well-funded and believe that great talent deserves great compensation. Full benefits (medical, vision, and dental) and flexible vacation policy (PTO). Remote-first team across many countries — You will be an early team member helping shape our vision, culture, and design practices. A+ colleagues — Our team includes alumni from: Goldman Sachs, Blackrock, Two Sigma, Bridgewater, SpaceX, AWS, Meta, Google, McKinsey, Circle, Uniswap. Best-in-class investors — We are proud to be backed by leading crypto experts and VCs, including Pantera Capital, Founders Fund and Coinbase Ventures.

title: Order to Cash Track Lead, Finance Engineering
description: At Klaviyo, we value the unique backgrounds, experiences and perspectives each Klaviyo (we call ourselves Klaviyos) brings to our workplace each and every day. We believe everyone deserves a fair shot at success and appreciate the experiences each person brings beyond the traditional job requirements. If you’re a close but not exact match with the description, we hope you’ll still consider applying. Want to learn more about life at Klaviyo? Visit klaviyo.com/careers  to see how we empower creators to own their own destiny. At Klaviyo, we know that building a great company starts with building a great team. We welcome candidates from a wide range of backgrounds and experiences, and we care as much about your trajectory and potential as we do about direct, one‑to‑one matches with every requirement. About the team Klaviyo went public in 2023 and is scaling fast. This is a rare chance to lead and build the Order to Cash (O2C) foundation for a company at this inflection point. The Finance Technology Systems team is part of G&A Systems within Global Technology Solutions (GTS). This group designs, operates, and continually improves the applications and workflows that power how Klaviyo manages money, risk, and financial reporting at scale. The team partners closely with Finance, Accounting, Tax, Treasury, FP&A, Procurement, and Internal Audit, as well as adjacent technology teams like Corporate IT, Data, and GTM Systems, to ensure our back‑office stack is reliable, well‑integrated, compliant, and ready for a public, AI‑forward SaaS business. We own the roadmap, health, and governance of platforms including our ERP and financial systems (e.g., NetSuite/Oracle), procure‑to‑pay (e.g., Coupa), revenue and billing systems, and related integrations and automation. This role reports to the Director, G&A Systems and leads the team responsible for Finance Technology Solutions across Klaviyo. What You'll Do As the Order to Cash (O2C) Lead, Finance Systems, you will be the accountable technology leader for Klaviyo’s O2C application landscape and core financial workflows. You will lead Enterprise and International Expansion capabilities that will provide revenue uplift for Klaviyo. Own the O2C track Execute on the roadmap for Klaviyo’s O2C stack aligned to the company priorities by translating business requirements into functional and technical design. Bring first principles thinking to your design. Integrate CPQ to NetSuite and ensure that all Enterprise capabilities are delivered with scale. Look at O2C systems landscape and provide recommendations to set Klaviyo for the future Ensure we deliver with the highest code quality by thoroughly thinking through test cases and applying rigorous build and test. Own SOX, controls, and audit readiness for Finance systems Own the design, implementation, and operation of IT General Controls (ITGCs) and other key controls across O2C applications, in partnership with Internal Audit, Security, and external auditors. Continually simplify and automate controls and evidence collection so audits are reliable and predictable, with fewer deficiencies and lower friction for Finance and GTS teams. Drive AI-native transformation across Finance  Lead Klaviyo's push to make Finance one of the most automated, insight-driven functions in the company. You'll identify and deliver high-value AI use cases across the O2C workflow.  You'll partner directly with Klaviyo's AI and data platform teams and Finance Engineering  to embed AI into core Finance processes with clear guardrails, measurable productivity gains, and the rigor expected of a public company. This isn't a future-state vision, it's work already underway, and you'll own it from a Product standpoint. Design and optimize core Finance processes and systems Have a leader mindset and partner with Controllership, Tax, Treasury  leaders to improve and continuously refine end‑to‑end O2C workflows ensuring systems and processes are tightly aligned. Ensure our ERP and other SaaS O2C applications are configured, integrated, and operated to support accurate, timely close, scalable revenue and billing, and high‑quality financial data that downstream teams can trust. Act as a strategic partner and communicator Serve as the primary technology partner for Controller, and Finance leadership team on systems, data, and process topics;  As needed, represent Finance Technology Systems in executive forums, planning cycles, and cross‑functional initiatives, ensuring O2C needs are anticipated and built into wider GTS and company roadmaps.
